subject: Seat + runtime blend proposal and migration risk recovery
messages:
From: Alex Cheng <alex@clearwayhealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Jill Ramos <jill.ramos@clearwayhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Partnership economics question: per-seat vs blended runtime model

Sean / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency profile looked really promising. Before we move to procurement, our finance team asked for a clearer view on two things that will drive our decision: 1) a per-seat license blended with runtime consumption for bursty usage, and 2) a migration / rollback credit in case production performance doesn’t meet the SLA during the first 90 days.

Concretely:
- Can you show a simple blended pricing worked example for 250 active seats with an estimated 1.2M tokens/month baseline and 800k tokens/month of burst traffic?
- What level of onboarding or rollback credit would Redwood consider for an initial 12-month commitment?
- Any constraints on data retention or KV cache sizes that would increase cost?

We’d like a written economics summary to share with procurement by next Wednesday. I attached our usage scenarios.

— Alex
Alex Cheng
Director of Product, Clearway Health
alex@clearwayhealth.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachments: usage-scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Alex Cheng <alex@clearwayhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partnership economics question: per-seat vs blended runtime model

Alex —

Thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. I pulled together a short note and looped Marissa (AM) and Karthik (solutions) to illustrate two practical packaging options: a Seat-first bundle and a Blended pool. High level: we can anchor on a modest onboarding credit that increases with committed term and usage guarantees; rollback credit is doable but we usually structure it as a refundable onboarding tranche tied to run-rate tests.

Quick sketches below (rough, will formalize into a one-pager):

1) Seat-first bundle (simpler for forecasting)
- 250 seats @ $60 seat/month = $15,000/mo base
- Includes 1.2M baseline tokens/month (pooled across seats)
- Usage overage: $0.0045 per token for first 1M overage, then $0.0036 for sustained months (>3 consecutive months)
- Onboarding credit: $50k applied against first 3 invoices; refundable tranche: up to $25k if SLA not met in first 90 days and customer completes defined remediation steps

2) Blended runtime pool (flex for bursty workloads)
- Base runtime commitment: $12,000/mo (reserved runtime), covers up to 1.2M tokens
- Seat license: $25 seat/month for access controls, admin, support = $6,250/mo
- Blended effective rate at baseline: ~ $0.014 per 1k tokens equivalent (includes seat overhead)
- Burst bucket pricing: pre-purchased burst credits at 35% discount to on-demand; dynamic throttles available to cap egress/burst costs
- Migration protection: if latency or success-rate targets miss SLO during onboarding, we credit up to 20% of the first quarter spend (applies to runtime portion only)

Operational notes:
- KV cache sizes above 10GB per deployment incur incremental fee tiers — call this out if you plan heavy multi-session contexts
- Egress is usage-metered in both models; we can include an egress inclusion in the seat-first bundle for an incremental fee (helps your predictable budget)

Marissa — can you confirm what level of discount on the base seat/license is needed to make option 1 attractive vs option 2 for their finance team? Karthik — can you validate the KV/cache thresholds against their usage workbook?

I’ll convert this into a short PDF and include a worked example for the numbers in the spreadsheet.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, Alex Cheng <alex@clearwayhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partnership economics question: per-seat vs blended runtime model

Alex — quick follow-up from the commercial side. A couple of negotiation points we typically see from customers in this profile:

- Multi-year term swaps more onboarding credit for a lower per-seat or baseline runtime rate. If Clearway goes 24 months we can tighten the step-down on overage pricing by ~12-18%.
- We can offer a migration services bucket (professional services hours) at a fixed rate that can be applied toward rollback remediation — prefer this to an unconditional cash refund as it ensures we fix root causes quickly.
- If procurement needs a line-item called "migration risk recovery" we can present it as a contingent credit applied only after a post-go-live benchmark is executed jointly.

Alex, two questions for you: 1) do you want a firm line in the quote for a refundable tranche or for PS hours? 2) Any legal restrictions around credits vs refunds for Clearway?

Monica — I’ll need a short onboarding level-of-effort estimate to include in the commercial workbook.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Alex Cheng <alex@clearwayhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Jill Ramos <jill.ramos@clearwayhealth.com>, procure@clearwayhealth.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partnership economics question: per-seat vs blended runtime model

Thanks Sean and Marissa — this is helpful. Procurement asked that we push back on two specific items:

1) They prefer a refundable cash credit rather than PS hours for migration risk recovery (they argued PS hours feel like "we have to use them").
2) They asked about a hard cap option: if monthly tokens exceed a predefined burst threshold, charges stop and we start throttling while we negotiate an emergency sustained-rate add-on. They want a clear escape hatch to prevent surprise bills while negotiations happen.

For now, please include both alternatives in the proposal (refundable tranche vs PS hours) and a hard cap option they can select during the first 6 months. Also: can you put the onboarding / rollback condition language in plain English so legal can evaluate quickly?

Two small clarifications on numbers: in the seat-first sketch, what drives the step-down to $0.0036 per token? Is that usage smoothing or a true volume tier?

If you can get a clean one-page quote by end of day Friday I’ll circulate to procurement and legal Monday.

— Alex

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Alex Cheng <alex@clearwayhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partnership economics question: per-seat vs blended runtime model

Alex — attached: a one-page quote and a short plain-English term sheet. Highlights:

- "Refundable tranche" option: $25k cash credit refundable if post-go-live SLO benchmark (latency, 99th perc success rate) misses target after 90 days; refund triggers after a joint analysis and customer-approved remediation attempt.
- "PS hours" option: 120 hours at a fixed rate, fully billable but convertible to credits if remediation is completed within the first 60 days.
- Hard cap option: yes — we’ll include a selectable hard cap with automatic throttling at +30% above baseline. If you hit the cap we pause on-demand billing and enter an agreed emergency add-on workflow.

On the step-down: $0.0036 is a sustained-volume tier that requires three consecutive months above the initial overage threshold; it’s intended as a discount for predictable high usage rather than short bursts. We’ll call that out explicitly.

Attachments: Clearway_RFP-response-v3.pdf (quote + term sheet), usage-scenarios.xlsx (worked numbers)

Next steps: Marissa will send a redline-ready quote; Karthik and Monica will review onboarding hours and cache assumptions. Alex — if you want, we can also model a 24-month variant with a larger onboarding tranche.

Thanks — talk Monday if needed.

Best,
Sean
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
